title: Pregnancy Symptoms to Never Ignore
hook: A few symptoms in pregnancy mean call your midwife or maternity unit straight away — they can signal serious problems like pre-eclampsia that need checking without delay.
key_points: A severe headache that won't ease with simple painkillers, or vision changes like blurring or flashing lights, need urgent checking.
Sudden swelling of the face, hands, or feet, or pain just below the ribs, can be signs of pre-eclampsia.
Vaginal bleeding, severe tummy pain, or your baby moving less than usual all warrant calling immediately — even overnight.
When in doubt, call your maternity unit or 111; it's always better to be checked than to wait.
content_html: Most pregnancy aches and niggles are normal, but a handful of symptoms are different: they mean contact your midwife or maternity unit straight away. Knowing them in advance saves precious time, because some — like pre-eclampsia — can develop quickly and need prompt treatment.
extra_html: According to the NHS, warning signs that need urgent attention include a severe headache that doesn't ease with simple painkillers, vision problems such as blurring or seeing flashing lights, sudden swelling of the face, hands, or feet, and pain just below the ribs — these can point to pre-eclampsia. Also call promptly for vaginal bleeding, severe tummy pain, or your baby moving less than usual. If you can't reach your maternity unit, call 111. This is general guidance — you can never be "too cautious" here, and your midwife or doctor would always rather check than have you wait.

related.title: Why Prenatal Visits Matter
related.hook: Regular checkups during pregnancy catch problems early — for many a typical schedule is monthly, then every two weeks, then weekly as the due date nears.

related.title: Warning Signs That Can't Wait
related.hook: Serious complications can happen during pregnancy and for up to a year after birth. Knowing the urgent warning signs — and insisting on being heard — can save a life.

related.title: The Common Aches of Pregnancy
related.hook: Nausea, heartburn, fatigue, and a sore back are the everyday companions of pregnancy — usually normal and manageable. The skill is knowing the simple fixes, and which symptoms are not on this list.

flashcards.prompt: Which combination of symptoms can be a warning sign of pre-eclampsia?

choices.text: Severe headache, vision changes, and sudden swelling of the face or hands
Feeling hungry and needing the toilet more often

flashcards.explanation_html: Severe headache, blurred or flashing vision, sudden swelling, and pain below the ribs can all signal pre-eclampsia and need checking right away.

flashcards.prompt: What should you do if your baby is moving less than usual?
flashcards.back_html: Call your midwife or maternity unit immediately — don't wait until the next day, even if it's the middle of the night. Reduced movement can be a sign of a problem.
